skill.description: Guidance for PyTorch Geometric graph neural networks, including datasets, GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, heterogeneous graphs, transforms, benchmarks, and visualizations.

skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found. The high eval findings are false positives because they call PyTorch model.eval(), and most filesystem and command alerts are documentation examples. One confirmed medium issue remains: the template generator writes to a user-supplied output path without overwrite or path validation.

remediation.suggestion: Validate output paths, avoid overwriting existing files unless explicitly confirmed, and limit generated files to a user-approved directory.
Prefer project-local cache directories in examples when persistence, isolation, or shared environments matter.

static_findings.snippet: 2. **Citation networks**: Planetoid datasets are perfect for node classification
PyG represents graphs using the `torch_geometric.data.Data` class with these key attributes:
- **`data.edge_index`**: Graph connectivity in COO format `[2, num_edges]`
- **`data.y`**: Target labels for nodes or graphs
Edges are stored in COO (coordinate) format as a `[2, num_edges]` tensor:
- A `batch` vector maps each node to its source graph
- **`message()`**: Constructs messages from source to target nodes
**Variable naming convention**: Appending `_i` or `_j` to tensor names automatically maps them to ta
For datasets that fit in memory, inherit from `InMemoryDataset`:
For large datasets that don't fit in memory, inherit from `Dataset` and implement `len()` and `get(i
For large graphs, use `NeighborLoader` to sample subgraphs:
For graphs with multiple node and edge types, use `HeteroData`:
Or use `HeteroConv` for custom edge-type-specific operations:
- **`references/layers_reference.md`**: Complete listing of all 40+ GNN layers with descriptions and
- **`references/datasets_reference.md`**: Comprehensive dataset catalog organized by category
- **`references/transforms_reference.md`**: All available transforms and their use cases
- **`references/api_patterns.md`**: Common API patterns and coding examples
- **`scripts/visualize_graph.py`**: Visualize graph structure using networkx and matplotlib
- **`scripts/create_gnn_template.py`**: Generate boilerplate code for common GNN architectures

content.value_statement: Graph neural network projects require many PyG patterns. This skill provides model, dataset, transform, benchmark, and visualization guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains PyTorch Geometric graph data structures and batching patterns.
Provides model guidance for GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GIN, and custom message passing layers.
Maps common PyG datasets to node, graph, molecular, temporal, and heterogeneous graph tasks.
Documents transforms for normalization, sampling, splitting, point clouds, meshes, and link prediction.
Includes utility scripts for graph visualization, benchmark runs, and generated GNN templates.
Covers training loops, evaluation workflows, GPU placement, pooling, and model explainability.
limitations: Does not replace version-specific PyTorch Geometric API documentation.
Does not train models unless a user runs the included scripts or generated code.
Assumes PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric, and required compiled dependencies are installed.
Benchmark examples may need changes for private datasets, large graphs, or production workloads.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Node Classifier
use_cases.description: Build a GCN, GAT, or GraphSAGE workflow for Cora, PubMed, or another citation network.

use_cases.title: Compare Graph Models
use_cases.description: Benchmark several GNN architectures and interpret training time, validation accuracy, and test accuracy.

use_cases.title: Prepare Graph Data
use_cases.description: Select PyG datasets, transforms, loaders, and split strategies for graph or molecular learning tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a PyG Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the torch-geometric skill to outline a PyG project for node classification on Cora. Include data loading, model choice, training, and evaluation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a GNN Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the torch-geometric skill to compare GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, and GIN for my graph task. Explain when each layer is a good fit.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Data Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the torch-geometric skill to design a PyG data pipeline for heterogeneous graph learning. Include datasets, transforms, loaders, masks, and evaluation metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a GNN Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the torch-geometric skill to review my PyG workflow for scalability, leakage risks, batching issues, transform placement, and reproducible benchmarking.

output_examples.input: User asks how to classify nodes in a citation graph.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a structured plan covering Planetoid data loading, a GCN baseline, masks, training steps, and accuracy reporting.

output_examples.input: User asks which PyG dataset fits molecular property prediction.
output_examples.output: The skill compares MoleculeNet, QM9, ZINC, and related datasets, then recommends choices based on target labels and graph size.

output_examples.input: User asks why a large graph workflow is slow.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests neighbor sampling, transform caching, GPU placement checks, and batch-size adjustments before deeper model changes.

best_practices: Start with a small benchmark dataset before moving to private or large-scale graph data.
Keep expensive preprocessing in pre-transforms and cheap augmentation in runtime transforms.
Track masks, splits, random seeds, and metrics so graph experiments remain reproducible.
anti_patterns: Do not compare GNN models with different data splits or untracked random seeds.
Do not apply test-set transforms or labels during training pipeline construction.
Do not load large full graphs when neighbor sampling or mini-batching is required.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users design, train, evaluate, and debug PyTorch Geometric graph neural network workflows.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include runnable scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes scripts for template generation, model benchmarking, and graph visualization.

faq.question: Can it handle heterogeneous graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents HeteroData, to_hetero, HeteroConv, and related dataset patterns.

faq.question: Does it install PyTorch Geometric?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but users must run installation commands themselves.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: It is best for guidance and prototypes. Production use needs dependency pinning, monitoring, and data governance.
